problem.text: How many of the first $2018$ numbers in the sequence $101, 1001, 10001, 100001, \ldots$ are divisible by $101$?

steps.title: Where to start: write the terms as powers of 10
steps.body: Each term is a $1$, some zeros, and a $1$, so it is a power of ten plus one: $101 = 10^2 + 1$, $1001 = 10^3 + 1$, and so on. Now the question becomes: for which exponents $n$ is $10^n + 1$ a multiple of $101$?

your_turn.prompt: The first term has $n = 2$. What is $n$ for the $2018$th term?
your_turn.answer: The exponent goes up by $1$ each term, so the $2018$th term is $10^{2019} + 1$. The exponents run from $2$ to $2019$.

steps.title: Track remainders when dividing by 101
steps.body:
We only care about the remainder of $10^n$ when divided by $101$. Write $a \equiv b \pmod{101}$ (read "$a$ is congruent to $b$ mod $101$") when $a - b$ is a multiple of $101$. The key fact is $100 = 101 - 1$, so $10^2 \equiv -1$. Multiplying by $10$ each time, the powers of $10$ go
$$10^0 \equiv 1,\quad 10^1 \equiv 10,\quad 10^2 \equiv -1,\quad 10^3 \equiv -10,\quad 10^4 \equiv 1, \ldots$$

your_turn.prompt: Why is $10^4 \equiv 1$? Check it with actual numbers.
your_turn.answer: $10^4 = 10^2 \cdot 10^2 \equiv (-1)(-1) = 1$. Indeed $10000 = 99 \cdot 101 + 1$. So the pattern repeats every $4$ steps.

steps.title: Which exponents work?
steps.body: $10^n + 1$ is a multiple of $101$ exactly when $10^n \equiv -1$, and that happens exactly when $n$ leaves remainder $2$ when divided by $4$. Careful: not every even exponent works. When $n$ is a multiple of $4$, $10^n \equiv 1$, so $10^n + 1$ leaves remainder $2$.

your_turn.prompt: Test it: is $10001$ divisible by $101$? And what are the smallest and largest exponents from $2$ to $2019$ that leave remainder $2$ when divided by $4$?
your_turn.answer: $10001 = 99 \cdot 101 + 2$, so no ($n = 4$ is a multiple of $4$). The exponents that work start at $2$ and end at $2018$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The good exponents are $2, 6, 10, \ldots, 2018$, going up by $4$. Count them:
$$\frac{2018 - 2}{4} + 1 = 504 + 1 = 505.$$
The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.B: $504$ comes from counting exponents that are multiples of $4$. For those, $10^n$ leaves remainder $1$, so $10^n + 1$ leaves remainder $2$ and is not divisible by $101$.
wrong_choices.E: $1009$ comes from thinking every even exponent works. Only half of them do: $10^4 + 1 = 10001$, for example, is not a multiple of $101$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
